thread.title_full: OKC police release bodycam video of June officer-involved shooting - NewsBreak

author: Spencer Humphrey/KFOR
title: OKC police release bodycam video of June officer-involved shooting - NewsBreak
text:
By Spencer Humphrey/KFOR ,
6 hours ago
OKLAHOMA CITY ( KFOR ) — Oklahoma City police released bodycam video Tuesday showing the moments an officer fired on a man police say allegedly pointed a gun at an officer during a June 23 standoff at an apartment complex off Northwest 10th.
Maine shooting and officer’s background raise new questions about ICE’s rapid hiring Officers responded to the complex around 7 p.m. after receiving reports of a man with a gun — 32-year-old Demetrius Wine.
Police had already responded to the same complex earlier that day after a separate disturbance complaint involving Wine, but did not find him at that time.
When the first officer arrived for the second call, she spotted Wine running through the complex, got out of her car and began chasing him.
“Show me your hands! Show me your hands! Show me your hands!” the officer can be heard shouting in the video as she ran toward an apartment building.
She cornered Wine outside a storm shelter building, where police say he pointed a gun at her.
“33 hold the air!” she called out — then immediately fired four shots toward the unoccupied storm shelter Wine was standing outside of.
Police say none of those shots hit anyone.
Wine ran back into his apartment, where police say he stayed inside for an hour and a half before officers coaxed him onto the porch.
“Hey Demetrius, will you walk out here a little further and talk to us?” an officer said over a loudspeaker. “You’re doing a good job, okay.”
Officers spent the next half minute trying to get Wine to walk over peacefully.
“Just calm down for us and walk out here and speak with us,” one officer said.
“Keep coming, you’re doing a good job,” another said. “Keep coming. Keep coming. You’re doing a good job Demetrius.”
Wine was tentative, taking a couple steps forward before stopping and stepping back.
“Hey keep coming, you’re alright,” an officer said. “Hey you’re okay.”
“Hey just come talk to us man,” another officer said.
“Come out here and talk to us,” a third officer said. “Come out here and talk to us.”
Eventually, a group of officers stepped in and fired a less-lethal weapon as well as a taser, knocking Wine to the ground and taking him into custody.
After being medically cleared, police booked Wine into the Oklahoma County Jail on charges of pointing a firearm, possession of a firearm after a felony conviction and possession of a controlled substance.
No officers or anyone else suffered injuries during the incident.
The officer involved is on routine administrative leave as the investigation continues.
